column3: “The voice of the words of the LORD” is shortened to “the words of the LORD.”
“I have paid attention to” is rendered “I will punish,” and “what he set to him” as “how he set himself against him.”
“Attack” is rendered “strike,” and “suckling child” as “infant.”
Close to the Hebrew.
“Wadi” is rendered “valley.”
“Loyalty” (Hebrew חֶסֶד) is rendered “kindness,” and “Amalek” as “the Amalekites.”
“Attacked” is rendered “defeated,” and “on the face of Egypt” as “east of Egypt.”
Close to the Hebrew; “mouth of the sword” is rendered “edge of the sword.”
“The second” (Hebrew וְהַמִּשְׁנִים) is rendered “the fatlings”; the meaning is uncertain.
Close to the Hebrew.
“My words” is rendered “My commands,” and “it burned to Samuel” as “Samuel was distressed.”
Close to the Hebrew.
“The word of the LORD” is rendered “the command of the LORD.”
“Sound of the sheep” and “sound of the cattle” are rendered “bleating” and “lowing.”
NASB supplies “They have brought them.”
“Be quiet” is rendered “Wait,” and “this night” as “last night.”
NASB supplies “Is it not true” and “you were made.”
“Journey” is rendered “mission,” and “until they destroy them” as “until they are exterminated.”
“Listen to the voice” is rendered “obey the voice.”
“I listened” is rendered “I did obey,” and “Amalek” as “the Amalekites.”
NASB supplies “some of,” and “objects for destruction” becomes “things devoted to destruction.”
“To pay attention” is rendered “to heed.”

The Hebrew is compact (“the sin of divination is rebellion, and wickedness and teraphim is presumption”). NASB renders “rebellion is as the sin of divination, and insubordination is as iniquity and idolatry.”
“The mouth of the LORD” is rendered “the command of the LORD”; NASB adds “indeed.”
“Bow down” is rendered “worship.”
Close to the Hebrew.
NASB names “Saul” as the one who seized the robe; the Hebrew has only “he.”
Close to the Hebrew; “He will give it” is rendered “has given it.”
“The eminence of Israel” is rendered “the Glory of Israel,” and “regret” as “change His mind.”
“Bow down” is rendered “worship.”
